findings.title: Flusher processes are not terminated in `join()` when timeout expires
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` checks `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before calling `process.terminate()`. If `self.next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting for an earlier flusher process consumes the entire timeout budget, the loop breaks out early and leaves all remaining flusher processes running instead of terminating them. Instead of breaking out of the loop, it should skip the `while process.is_alive()` wait and still call `process.terminate()` on each remaining alive process.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard` in `SpanFlusher.main`
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.main`, `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 195) use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` (line 199) uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural). This makes the tag key inconsistent across flusher metrics.

findings.title: `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` is a no-op because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched
findings.body: Line 15 monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 (intended to give flusher threads time to process after the drift change) does nothing and returns immediately, which can make the test flaky.
